input:
This executive summary presents an overview of delivery performance at a contract packaging firm that operates 4 plants and generates revenue of $113 million per year. The evidence base for this assessment comprises order records covering 12 months and 15753 orders. Over the last two quarters, on-time delivery stood at 86%, which falls considerably short of the target of 95% and represents a significant area of concern for the business.

The data show that the problem is heavily concentrated in one location, since Plant 2 accounts for no less than 59% of all late orders. Overtime cost amounted to $1.9 million last year, an increase of 18% on the year before, while the order backlog currently stands at 2.9 weeks, compared with just 2 weeks a year ago. A scheduling system has been quoted at $339k for installation across all plants, or $130k for Plant 2 alone. An internal estimate, which is not a vendor figure, suggests that the scheduling system could reduce overtime at Plant 2 by some 15-20% in the first year.

The recommendation under consideration is therefore to install the system at Plant 2 first, at a cost of $130k, and to hold the other plants until the results at Plant 2 have been reported and evaluated. This phased approach would allow the business to validate the benefits at the plant where the need is greatest, where 59% of late orders originate, before committing to the full expenditure. The scheduling programme is owned by the operations director, who will oversee its implementation and report on progress.
